description: Erection of basement and ground floor rear extension.
decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

<p>Tree and ground protection for all retained trees at the site shall be undertaken in accordance with BS5837:2012 (Trees in relation to construction - Recommendations) and will protect the Root Protection Area (RPA) calculated as described in Table 2 of that British Standard for the duration of all site works (including demolition) undertaken in connection with the development hereby approved.<br style="">1. Protective Fencing<br style="">The protective fencing will be 2.4m high and conform to Figure 2 of BS5837:2012, i.e. a scaffold framework comprising a vertical and horizontal framework, well braced to resist impacts, with vertical tubes spaced at a maximum interval of 3m. On to this weldmesh panels should be securely fixed with wire or scaffold clamps. Suitable analogues such as boundary walls or fences may be acceptable if adequately robust.<br style="">2. Temporary Ground Protection within the RPA<br style="">Where construction access is required within the RPA, new temporary ground protection shall be implemented and maintained. This protection must be capable of supporting any traffic entering or using the site without being distorted or causing compaction of the underlying soil within the RPA. The ground protection used shall be selected based on the anticipated traffic loading:<br style="">a) For Pedestrian Movements Only: A single thickness of scaffold boards placed either on top of a driven scaffold frame, so as to form a suspended walkway, or on top of a compression-resistant layer (e.g., 100 mm depth of woodchip), laid onto a geotextile membrane.<br style="">b) For Pedestrian-Operated Plant (up to 2 t gross weight): Proprietary, inter-linked ground protection boards placed on top of a compression-resistant layer (e.g., 150 mm depth of woodchip), laid onto a geotextile membrane.<br style="">c) For Wheeled or Tracked Construction Traffic (exceeding 2 t gross weight): An alternative system (e.g., proprietary systems or pre-cast reinforced concrete slabs) to an engineering specification designed in conjunction with arboricultural advice, to accommodate the likely loading to which it will be subjected.<br style=""><br style="">REASON: To comply with Section 197(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, and to ensure the long-term health and survival of retained trees by protecting their root systems from damage and soil compaction.<br></p>
